notes: Adaptive semantic LLM mode enabled via TKNT_SEMANTIC_ADAPTIVE_LLM; deterministic stage fallbacks are disabled.
Added a dedicated window_reading cluster because the brief explicitly requests a reading chair near a window and prioritizes window view/daylight.
Kept the object program minimal and preserved existing cluster ids where possible.
Tier hints are set to support deterministic keep/drop selection with realistic bedroom capacity and clear-center bias.

Bedroom is 16.95 m2 with strong center-openness bias, so sleep_core and storage_core should survive deterministically; keep one primary storage anchor and avoid over-pruning small support items when surplus exists.
Window-facing reading support is coherent with the brief and daylight regions, but should remain conditional on surplus; prefer a compact armchair and treat lamp/side table as secondary.
Work/study is plausible but not brief-primary; keep only if the planner has comfortable surplus after bed and wardrobe/dresser are placed.
Media and utility clusters are not supported by the brief and should usually be filtered out.
Preserve clear entry landing and center circulation.
Keep bed and wardrobe on wall-backed/privacy-favored zones; avoid blocking windows.
Daylit seating/work can share window-adjacent wall segments if circulation remains open.
Planner output is cluster/bundle/zone level only; pose is left to downstream composer and solver.
Style policy compiled before layout planning; downstream geometry treats it as bias, not a hard override.
Request contract attached before tier count so explicit functional objects are protected from silent pruning.
Tier Count used deterministic utility, capacity, and bundle-preserving rules, plus Forge semantic tier-count hints when available.
Tier Count itself did not run an additional LLM call.
Output is synchronized for the object-level anchor-first solver handoff.
Merged into solver-ready object program for object-level anchor-first placement.
Bedroom correction raised restfulness and clutter control.
